## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 7/10** · likely safe to merge New, well-tested services, but KV/R2 calls are invisible and one sweep/incident path each lack coverage or a signal. 1 warning −1 · 4 notes · tests partial −1 · risk medium · 3/4 new units observable −1 Adds the status page backend: page/component/incident service, snapshot builder, KV+R2 publisher and break-glass reconciler, driven by a new alerting cron tick. Safe to merge once the store's KV/R2 calls get spans and the incident listing is bounded. The ten open errors in `apps/alerting/src/scheduled.ts` are pre-existing PlanetScale/warehouse/chat failures reached through the Worker entry, and this diff neither causes nor fixes any of them. - `statusPagesTick` runs reconcile, auto-incident repair and publish on the escalation lane - `StatusPagePublisher.sweep` publishes due pages and drains edge cleanups - `StatusPageStore` reads/writes snapshots, routes and break-glass entries in KV + R2 - `AlertsService` opens/resolves status page incidents for uptime alerts ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F5 · In-progress maintenance is never asserted, though it paints components maintenance tests · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.test.ts:116-127`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/6bdd42438bb120879349a121af9986168fcf6936/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.test.ts#L116-L127) The only maintenance case is `status: "scheduled"`, which `isListedIncident` handles by time window and which is never active; `isActiveIncident` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:279`) treats `kind: "maintenance", status: "in_progress"` as active and `incidentComponentStatus` returns `"maintenance"` for it. Deleting that branch passes the whole suite. ``` Add a case with `incident({ kind: "maintenance", status: "in_progress" })` and assert it is listed and its component's status is `"maintenance"`. ```
🔵 Note · F1 · KV and R2 calls have no Client span or peer.service observability · MAP-02 · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageStore.ts:150-157`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/6bdd42438bb120879349a121af9986168fcf6936/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageStore.ts#L150-L157) Every store operation funnels through `call`'s `Effect.tryPromise` (`StatusPageStore.ts:214`), so the alerting Worker's KV and R2 traffic — the whole point of the publisher — never appears on the service map, only as gap time inside the sweep span. The repo already sets `peer.service` on outbound calls (`packages/backend/src/platform/Apns.ts:311`). ``` Wrap each backend call in a Client span annotated with `peer.service` (`cloudflare-kv` / `cloudflare-r2`) and `db.collection.name`-style key prefix, inside `call`. ```
🔵 Note · F2 · listIncidents reads a page's whole incident history with no limit performance · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:932-942`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/6bdd42438bb120879349a121af9986168fcf6936/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts#L932-L942) With `includeResolved: true` (StatusPagesService.ts:928) the query has no `limit`, and `loadIncidents` (`StatusPagesService.ts:356`) then materialises every component link and every update row for all of those incidents. A long-lived page returns its entire history and update log in one response. ``` Add keyset pagination on `startedAt`/`id` to the incidents query and cap the links/updates load to the returned id window. ```
🔵 Note · F3 · Sweep publish and cleanup failures are counted nowhere alertable observability · MET-02 · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagePublisher.ts:294-296`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/6bdd42438bb120879349a121af9986168fcf6936/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagePublisher.ts#L294-L296) `failed` and `cleanupsFailed` reach only a return value and the tick's log line, so a page failing every sweep (KV or R2 down, `lastPublishError` set) serves a stale snapshot with no counter to alert on, while the alerting Worker already exports counters (`packages/backend/src/observability/AlertingMetrics.ts`). ``` Add `statuspages.publish_failures_total` and `statuspages.cleanup_failures_total` counters keyed by `error._tag` next to the existing `Effect.logWarning`. ```
🔵 Note · F4 · Auto incident sync failure is logged with no org, rule or incident id observability · LOG-03 · [`packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AlertsService.ts:671-676`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/6bdd42438bb120879349a121af9986168fcf6936/packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AlertsService.ts#L671-L676) The swallow in `syncStatusPages` records only `error.message`, so a dropped open or resolve cannot be tied to the rule, alert incident or status page it lost — the one line the operator gets from a page that silently never opened an incident. ``` Thread the identifiers into `syncStatusPages` and annotate `orgId`, `maple.alert.rule_id`, `maple.alert.incident_id` and the affected `maple.status_page.id` values on the warning. ```

Component positions can collide after a delete. It does not touch the PlanetScale, warehouse, chat or delivery errors already reported from `apps/alerting/src/scheduled.ts`; the new tick is isolated per step and leaves them as they are. - `StatusPagePublisher.sweep` drains cleanups, republishes due pages, then writes the heartbeat - `StatusPageReconciler` imports break-glass KV entries idempotently on the `overlay_entry_id` claim - Uptime alert incidents open and resolve page incidents after the alert commit - Alerting Worker binds `StatusSnapshotsKv` and `StatusSnapshotsBucket`; status work rides the escalation lane ### Before merge - [ ] **Manual** · Deploy the infra so the alerting Worker actually gets `StatusSnapshotsKv` and `StatusSnapshotsBucket` bindings before the escalation lane runs the status page tick ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F6 · position: existing.length reuses a live component's position after a delete correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:787`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/427e189c1e2f74fcd08b7685899e737429507482/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts#L787) Positions are not re-packed on delete, so with positions 0 and 2 left after removing the middle component a new component is inserted at `position: 2` and shares it. The tie is then broken differently on each side: `selectComponents` orders by `position, createdAt, id` (line 746) while the published snapshot orders by `position, id` (`StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:285`), so the admin list and the public page show those two components in different, essentially arbitrary orders. Use `max(position) + 1` over `existing` (or re-pack positions in the same transaction) instead of the row count. ``` position: existing.reduce((max, c) => Math.max(max, c.position), -1) + 1, ```
🟠 Warning · F7 · Span name built from a runtime value observability · TEL-03 · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageStore.ts:226`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/427e189c1e2f74fcd08b7685899e737429507482/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageStore.ts#L226) The span name `StatusPageStore.${operation}` is built from a runtime value, so every value becomes its own operation: grouping, rollups and alerts by span name stop working. Keep the name fixed and put the value in an attribute.

🟠 Warning · F8 · Status-page write is awaited inline before pushIncidentNotification performance · [`packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AlertsService.ts:3151-3161`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/cbca508c9daecc1fe31ed399ba04fceea17a8342/packages/backend/src/services/alerts/AlertsService.ts#L3151-L3161) `syncStatusPages` runs synchronously between the incident insert and `pushIncidentNotification` (`AlertsService.ts:3175`), so a status-page transaction that waits on a lock holds the alert tick before the page goes out, and a write that outlasts the lane deadline interrupts the lane and drops the notification for that rule and every rule after it in the batch. The comment on `syncStatusPages` (`AlertsService.ts:658`) claims the opposite. ``` Fork the already-caught program (`yield* Effect.forkDaemon(syncStatusPages(...))`) so the tick reaches `pushIncidentNotification` without waiting on the status-page transaction, or bound it with `Effect.timeout`. ```

> [!WARNING]
> **In-progress maintenance is never asserted, though it paints components `maintenance`**
>
> <sub>F5 · Warning · tests</sub>

The only maintenance case is `status: "scheduled"`, which `isListedIncident` handles by time window and which is never active; `isActiveIncident` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:279`) treats `kind: "maintenance", status: "in_progress"` as active and `incidentComponentStatus` returns `"maintenance"` for it. Deleting that branch passes the whole suite.

```
Add a case with `incident({ kind: "maintenance", status: "in_progress" })` and assert it is listed and its component's status is `"maintenance"`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`position: existing.length` reuses a live component's position after a delete**
>
> <sub>F6 · Warning · correctness</sub>

Positions are not re-packed on delete, so with positions 0 and 2 left after removing the middle component a new component is inserted at `position: 2` and shares it. The tie is then broken differently on each side: `selectComponents` orders by `position, createdAt, id` (line 746) while the published snapshot orders by `position, id` (`StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:285`), so the admin list and the public page show those two components in different, essentially arbitrary orders. Use `max(position) + 1` over `existing` (or re-pack positions in the same transaction) instead of the row count.

```
position: existing.reduce((max, c) => Math.max(max, c.position), -1) + 1,
```

```suggestion
																				position: existing.reduce((max, c) => Math.max(max, c.position), -1) + 1,
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Span name built from a runtime value**
>
> <sub>F7 · Warning · observability · TEL-03</sub>

The span name `StatusPageStore.${operation}` is built from a runtime value, so every value becomes its own operation: grouping, rollups and alerts by span name stop working. Keep the name fixed and put the value in an attribute.

> [!WARNING]
> **Status-page write is awaited inline before `pushIncidentNotification`**
>
> <sub>F8 · Warning · performance</sub>

`syncStatusPages` runs synchronously between the incident insert and `pushIncidentNotification` (`AlertsService.ts:3175`), so a status-page transaction that waits on a lock holds the alert tick before the page goes out, and a write that outlasts the lane deadline interrupts the lane and drops the notification for that rule and every rule after it in the batch. The comment on `syncStatusPages` (`AlertsService.ts:658`) claims the opposite.

```
Fork the already-caught program (`yield* Effect.forkDaemon(syncStatusPages(...))`) so the tick reaches `pushIncidentNotification` without waiting on the status-page transaction, or bound it with `Effect.timeout`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **A failed or timed-out auto-incident open is never retried**
>
> <sub>F10 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`syncStatusPages` swallows the open failure and rolls the transaction back, and the only repair path, `repairOrphanedAutoIncidents` (`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/auto-incidents.ts:203`), resolves page incidents — it never opens a missing one. Since this is the single call site of `openForAlertIncident`, an incident whose write loses to the 3 second timeout never appears on the page: it reads `operational` for the whole outage, contrary to the comment at line 663 that the repair sweep catches up.

```
Have the repair sweep also open the status page incidents of alert incidents that are still open with no page incident (re-running `openForAlertIncident` is idempotent), or drop the "repair sweep catches up" claim and retry the open once after the failed write.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`repairMissingAutoIncidents` full-scans `alert_incidents` on every tick**
>
> <sub>F12 · Warning · performance</sub>

The cross-org repair filters `a.first_triggered_at >= ...` and `a.status <> 'resolved'` with no org predicate, and every index on `alert_incidents` is org-prefixed (`packages/db/src/tables/alerts.ts:224-227`), so Postgres has no index to use and scans the whole incident table — which only grows — on each minute's status-page tick. The join `m.alert_rule_id = a.rule_id` is equally unindexed (`packages/db/src/tables/uptime.ts:39-40`), so it adds a full scan of `uptime_monitors` too.

```
Add `PG.index("alert_incidents_first_triggered_idx", ["firstTriggeredAt"])` to `AlertIncidents` and `PG.index("uptime_monitors_alert_rule_idx", ["alertRuleId"])` to `UptimeMonitors`, then regenerate with `bun run --cwd packages/db db:generate --name status-page-auto-incident-repair`.
```
